catalog_quote: Stress in Shughni is not lexically contrastive and almost always falls on the final syllable in multisyllabic words. ... However, word stress is relatively weak and is generally subordinate to phrasal stress (Edelman & Yusufbekov 2000; Edelman & Dodykhudoeva 2009b). In polymorphemic words, stress can end up on non-final syllables, with (i) derivational affixes, (ii) inflectional affixes, and (iii) case-like suffixes and morphophonological clitics all behaving differently with regard to stress. The vast majority of derivational suffixes attract stress, while most if not all derivational prefixes do not attract stress. Inflectional affixes, on the other hand, seem to be lexically specified for stress: plural suffixes and verbal negation prefixes are stressed, while verbal agreement suffixes are unstressed. new_statements.rule_in_words: Default word-final stress: in monomorphemic multisyllabic words stress falls on the last syllable and is not contrastive. Stress-attracting morphology (most derivational suffixes, plural suffixes, comparative -di, locative -aǰ) keeps stress final; but a class of morphemes never carries stress (derivational prefixes, present-tense person-number agreement suffixes, case-like suffixes -ti/-and/-ard/-va/-ec, second-position person and =ta clitics), so stress stays on the last stress-attracting syllable of the base; in the present-tense verb stress is on the stem-final syllable, and the negation prefixes na- (indicative) and mā- (prohibitive/subjunctive) take primary stress. The earlier in-repo reading of Edelman & Dodykhudoeva 2009 flagged this as morphology-conditioned (S2-outside the catalog's scope); Parker's wording supports a fixed: final syllable default with morphologically specified unstressed/stressed affixes.
new_statements.secondary_stress: p. 74: when a negation prefix na-/mā- is present, 'primary stress in the verbal complex is on the negation prefix, and the final syllable of the verb stem receives secondary stress (Edelman & Yusufbekov 2000: 228)', e.g. násàwi 'you don't go', mā́sā̀wi, nafirā̀pi, māfirā̀pi.
new_statements.exceptions: Monomorphemic initial-stress exceptions xúbaθ 'self (emph)', áraj 'three', nála (direct-speech particle) (fn. 4, after Olson 2017); adverb-forming suffix -aθ does not attract stress (sārakíyaθ); borrowed prefixes be-, ba-, no- unstressed; Arabic loans with unstressed epenthetic -i keep penultimate stress (úmri, fī́kri, náqli); Russian loans usually keep Russian stress (pirímerna) or drop the final unstressed vowel (pičén).
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level stress; the author states word stress is 'relatively weak and is generally subordinate to phrasal stress' and that acoustic properties have not been examined; the present-tense verbal complex follows its own rule (stem-final stress, negation prefix primary). Basis: author's fieldwork with Shughni consultants plus Soviet-era descriptions (Edelman & Yusufbekov 2000; Edelman & Dodykhudoeva 2009).
new_statements.identity_note: Parker 2023 describes Shughni proper (shug1248; ISO sgh), the Khorog-area variety of Tajik Badakhshan with consultants' dialect variation noted; Glottolog's shug1248 reference list also carries grammars of sister varieties in the Shughni-Rushani group (Karamxudoev 1973 Bartangi, Kurbanov et al. 1976 Roshorvi, Fajzov 1966 Rushani, Mirzabdinova 1983 Khufi, Karamshoev 1963 Bajuw dialect), which are not the variety quoted here.
